message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

Analyzing the game state. I have $77 cash and my position shows JAIL but in_jail is false. This appears to be a post-turn action decision.

I have the orange monopoly but New York Avenue is mortgaged. I also own Water Works and Marvin Gardens. I am weighing whether to mortgage a property, propose a trade, or end my turn.

p2 has $540 and is weak. p3 has $397, is in jail, and owns hotels on the dark blue set plus mortgaged railroads and utilities.

p4 has $3251 and owns light blue hotels, the pink set, and several railroads. They lack the pink and yellow monopolies that I hold.

I will keep Marvin Gardens and the pink properties to avoid completing monopolies for p4. I cannot unmortgage any properties right now.

I cannot unmortgage New York Avenue because it costs $110 and I only have $77. I will not mortgage properties preemptively. I am checking standard mortgage values for my other holdings.

Mortgaging all six properties would raise $535, bringing total cash to $612. That covers a $600 hotel hit. Pre-mortgaging would sacrifice rent income and future interest payments. I am now considering whether to trade.

I cannot build on the orange monopoly because I lack the $110 to unmortgage New York Avenue and the $77 cash to buy houses. I am now considering trading with p3 or p2 to raise cash, since p3 has $397 and is in jail.

Selling Marvin Gardens to p2 would not complete a monopoly for them. Selling it to p4 would complete the yellow set and severely damage my position. I will not trade away any orange monopoly pieces.

I am now calculating the exact rent I would pay if I roll a 4 from Jail and land on Virginia. I also noted that p3 could flip any pink properties I trade to them toward p4.

Rolling from Jail is mostly safe. Virginia costs $12, Pennsylvania RR costs $50, and New York Avenue is mortgaged so it collects no rent. I am now looking for a trade that improves my position.

Developing the orange monopoly is impossible with only $77. It would require roughly $1,600 to unmortgage New York Avenue and build hotels. p4 has the cash but will not fund my development. p2 and p3 together cannot afford it either.

I cannot complete the red or green monopolies. p3 owns Indiana and Illinois, but they are mortgaged, and p4 holds Kentucky. The green set is split three ways. p4 holds three of the four yellow properties and will never sell one to me.

I rejected trading my pink properties to p4 because that would complete their pink monopoly and fund the leader. I also dismissed bankrupting p4 as unrealistic.

Instead, I am now considering selling Water Works to p2 for cash. This would let me unmortgage New York Avenue, which costs $110 and is currently blocking my orange development.

I rejected the Water Works trade. It would not raise enough cash to develop the orange monopoly meaningfully, and a utility monopoly would only slightly hurt me when I land there.

I also decided against selling anything to p3 for cash. Pre-selling would reduce my rent income, and p3 is unlikely to go broke from light blue hotels right now.

The correct play is to end my turn. I will not pre-mortgage, sell blockers, or fund p4.
